correctness.rationale: PASS subject to the actual published structural lemmas. The source proves a composite T-Fermat n is an odd squarefree Carmichael number, p<d(n)=2^M for every p|n, ν₂(p−1) equal over p, and all mutual ord_{p−1}(q) odd. Therefore its M distinct prime divisors form an M-clique in the explicit FINITE graph of primes <2^M at common ν₂. Independently rebuilt graph without using the supplied order algorithm: odd order iff gcd(q,p−1)=1 and q^{oddpart(phi(p−1))}=1 mod(p−1). Reproduced all per-M vertex/edge data, no M-cliques for 3≤M≤14, exactly one 15-clique (331,631,751,991,2311,4951,7351,11251,11551,14851,17011,25411,26251,28351,30871), whose product N fails Korselt at (N−1) mod 330=90. M≤2 excluded for composite Carmichael. This is exhaustive finite exclusion due p<2^M, not an inference from sampling or a claim for M≥16.
